name: farkle-r4
context:
ROUND 4 — run under EINCOL, which required measuring before generating and falsifying my own finding in writing. A Monte Carlo harness was built first and everything below is recomputed from seeds. Fifty changes follow the evidence.

─────────── STEP 1 · WHAT THE HARNESS MEASURED ───────────

Agent ladder, 400 seeds, 10 turns:

  GREEDY          0     farkle 100%   (never banks, so keeps nothing)
  EFFICIENT       0     farkle 100%
  RANDOM       4565     farkle 36.6%
  PRUDENT     16255     farkle  0.0%
  HUMAN-CAL*  17486     farkle 20.3%   (*uncalibrated stub, named blocker)
  SEARCH-24   18938     farkle  0.0%
  SEARCH-MAX  19942     farkle  0.0%

  SKILL DELTA    22.7%  against a ~5% industry benchmark
  SOLVER MARGIN   5.3%  unbounded over bounded search
  SEED SHARE OF VARIANCE  1.6%   (between-seed 1.28e6, between-policy 7.85e7)

That last number is the strongest result here and I did not expect it: on a shared seed, 98.4% of the variance in outcome comes from WHO IS PLAYING rather than WHAT WAS DEALT. For a staked shared-board mode that is the fairness property the whole settlement design needs, and it is measured rather than argued.

─────────── STEP 2 · THE DISTRIBUTION, AND THE TAIL I WORKED ───────────

The degenerate-strategy probe returned something alarming: `bank-after-1` — a mindless rule that takes the biggest chain and stops — scored 18742 against SEARCH-24's 18912. NINETY-NINE POINT ONE PERCENT OF THE BEST THOUGHTFUL AGENT, FOR NO THOUGHT.

Candidates for why, with honest priors:

  0.30  the turn cap binds; ten turns times one chain is most of the score
  0.20  the first chain of a fresh hand is by far the biggest, so continuations are worth little
  0.15  my risk model over-penalises and the agents bank too readily
  0.12  scoring is linear in chains taken, so nothing rewards a long run
  0.10  a free hand every turn removes any reason to squeeze one
  0.08  the big combos need six cells, so after the first chain only singles remain
  0.05  THE GAME HAS NO MECHANISM MAKING A LONG TURN WORTH MORE THAN MANY SHORT ONES

The tail row is the one that maps onto real Farkle. Tabletop has UNLIMITED turns and a target of 10,000, so what matters is points per turn and pushing is how you get them. Here turns are capped at ten, which makes points-per-turn trivially maximised by banking instantly. The structure that creates the decision had been removed without anyone noticing.

─────────── STEP 3+4 · I FALSIFIED MY OWN FINDING, AND THE CORRECTION IS BETTER ───────────

I stated the claim as 'the push decision is worthless because reward is linear', and went looking for the case it gets wrong. I found it.

Sweeping the best FIXED stop-depth, 500 seeds, scores in thousands:

  curve     d1     d2     d3     d4     d5     d6     d7    best
  flat     18.5   20.6   15.2    8.2    3.3    1.1    0.2    d2
  x1.15    18.5   23.7   20.0   12.5    5.7    2.2    0.5    d2
  x1.25    18.5   25.7   23.7   16.1    8.0    3.4    0.8    d2
  x1.35    18.5   27.8   27.6   20.2   10.8    4.9    1.3    d2
  x1.50    18.5   30.9   34.1   27.8   16.5    8.4    2.4    d3

THE CLAIM WAS WRONG. Even at flat reward the optimum is d2 at 20.6k, not d1 at 18.5k — pushing once is worth ELEVEN PERCENT. The decision was never dead.

What was actually wrong is my SEARCH-24 AGENT. It scored 18.9k where a two-chain fixed rule scores 20.6k, so a mindless rule came within 1% of it because THE THOUGHTFUL AGENT WAS BAD, not because the game was. I had been about to redesign a game around a defect in my own evaluator. Both versions are recorded because the first one is the evidence the process is real.

The corrected finding is sharper. Convexity does not create the decision; it controls HOW MUCH THE DECISION MATTERS and WHERE THE OPTIMUM SITS:

  flat   d2 beats d1 by 11%, and d3 is 26% WORSE than d2 — so 'push exactly once' is itself a fixed rule
  x1.35  d2 = 27.8k and d3 = 27.6k, TIED WITHIN 0.7%
  x1.50  the optimum moves out to d3

At x1.35 the two best depths are statistically indistinguishable ON AVERAGE, which means the correct depth cannot be read off a table — it has to come from the particular hand in front of you. That is precisely where judgement lives, and it is the measured argument for the multiplier rather than an aesthetic one.

─────────── THE FIFTY CHANGES ───────────

BALANCE (1-10)
1 A RUN MULTIPLIER of x1.35 per chain banked together, applied to the whole run. 2 Chosen because it makes depth 2 and depth 3 tie within 0.7%, not because it felt good. 3 The multiplier is displayed BEFORE the player commits, never revealed after. 4 Re-sweep the curve whenever the pay table changes; the constant is downstream of it. 5 FIX THE SEARCH AGENT — it is currently beaten by a two-chain fixed rule and every 'is this balanced' claim rests on it. 6 Add a fixed-depth rung (d1..d5) to the ladder permanently, because it caught what the search agent hid. 7 Keep turns capped at 10; the cap is what makes each turn's decision matter. 8 Do not tune the pay table; it is ported and parity is the contract. 9 Balance knobs are limited to hand size and run multiplier, both swept. 10 Every knob carries the sweep that chose it, in the file.

FAIRNESS (11-17)
11 Shared seed for VS, verified identical hands. 12 Blind settlement — no opponent total until both close. 13 Report SEED SHARE OF VARIANCE as a shipping gate; 1.6% now, must stay under 15%. 14 The server replays the input log; the client never submits a score. 15 Commit-reveal on the server seed with constant-time compare. 16 Pari-mutuel settles on RANK, so no scoring-scale change can alter who wins. 17 Publish the pay table and the multiplier curve in the rules screen.

EXPLOIT REMOVAL (18-24)
18 The degenerate probe runs in CI with named trivial rules, not just an agent ladder. 19 Add `always-max-multiplier` and `bank-at-risk-threshold` families to it. 20 A trivial rule within 2% of the best thoughtful agent FAILS the build. 21 Illegal chains forfeit the turn rather than being ignored, so a fuzzer gains nothing. 22 No client-supplied numbers anywhere in the action type. 23 Move clock bounds solver advantage; SOLVER MARGIN is 5.3% and is a gate. 24 The forecast stays depth-2 with row 2 fallible, so the board is not a solvable search.

GAME LOOP (25-31)
25 The turn is: draw hand, trace, decide, repeat, bank or farkle. 26 Hot streak: the multiplier is the reason to continue, replacing the cut hot-dice bonus. 27 A farkle loses the run AND the multiplier, which is what makes the multiplier a stake rather than a gift. 28 Turn summary on bank: chains, multiplier, total, one line. 29 Run length is the session's story, so the end screen reports the longest run. 30 No timers on the decision in solo. 31 A move clock only in VS, and only because it bounds the solver.

JUICE, POP AND REWARD (32-41)
32 The multiplier is the dopamine object: it ticks up visibly and audibly on every chain. 33 Each tick raises pitch — a rising marimba line, matter band, 260-520 Hz. 34 The pitch rise IS the tension; no other sound escalates. 35 Chain trace plays one note per die, pitched by face, so a chain is a melody. 36 Banking resolves the melody to a chord; a farkle drops it an octave and stops. 37 Screen shake never. Scale-punch on the banked total instead, 120 ms. 38 Spent cells collapse rather than fade, so the hand visibly shrinks. 39 Combo name arrives on the beat of the last die, not on release. 40 Haptic: one tick per die, one thud on bank, silence on farkle. 41 Reduced-motion replaces every animation with a state change, and the audio still carries the loop.

HD POLISH (42-46)
42 Dice render at device pixel ratio with integer-snapped positions. 43 The lit lip and the matter body give a die material at any scale. 44 The hand outline is a single traced path, so it stays crisp at 3x. 45 Type at 393px is the design size; nothing is scaled up from smaller. 46 A frame budget gate: p99 frame cost under 16.67 ms at 4x CPU throttle, currently 3.20 ms.

MODES (47-50)
47 SOLO: ten turns, score is the bank, the longest run is the badge. 48 VS: shared seed, blind settlement, move clock, pari-mutuel on rank. 49 COOP: one board, alternating turns, SEPARATE banks — the shared resource is the board, not the score. 50 Coop scores the PAIR by their combined bank but ranks pairs against pairs, so stranding your partner costs you without letting you lose their points.

─────────── WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED ───────────

HUMAN-CAL is an uncalibrated stub and is reported as one. No audio exists yet, so every claim in 32-41 is a design intent rather than a result. The coop pair-ranking in 50 has not been simulated at all.

questions.text: I claimed the push decision was worthless, then falsified it myself: the real defect was that my search agent was beaten by a two-chain fixed rule. Does that change of diagnosis hold, or am I now over-correcting and excusing a genuine design problem by blaming the evaluator?

A x1.35 run multiplier makes depth 2 and depth 3 tie within 0.7% on average. Is 'the two best options are statistically tied' actually where judgement lives, or does it just mean the choice does not matter?
98.4% of outcome variance comes from the policy rather than the seed. Is that the right measure of fairness for a shared-board staked game, or does it hide an asymmetry it cannot see?
Which of the fifty is most likely to be cargo-cult — present because a polished game usually has it, rather than because this game needs it?
Name the single strongest reason this set of changes would still leave the game unsatisfying to play.
